kaps_punt: diere skuilings kan natuurlik wees insluitende neste, skulpe, hol bome, perdeby nes of mensgemaakte hondehokke, hokke, krale, stalle; diereskuilings kan dop- of raamstrukture wees, kan verskillende vorms en groottes hê, en kan gemaak word van verskillende materiale

items.bewering: 'n Skuiling is 'n plek waar 'n dier veilig kan wees. Baie skuilings hou die reën en die koue van hom af. Hulle hou hom ook weg van diere wat hom wil vang.
items.bron: Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources, 'What is habitat? Shelter can protect wildlife' (dwr.virginia.gov): shelter is a place to escape harsh weather and hide from predators. Texas Parks and Wildlife, 'Animal homes: background for teachers' (tpwd.texas.gov), says the same.

items.bewering: Baie diere maak hul kleintjies binne 'n skuiling groot.
items.bron: Virginia DWR (dwr.virginia.gov): shelter includes a secure place to raise young. The quantifier 'baie' is correct; not every animal does this.

items.bewering: 'n Skuiling is nie dieselfde ding as 'n habitat nie. 'n Habitat is die hele plek waar 'n dier leef, en 'n skuiling is een plek daarin.
items.bron: Vocabulary.com, 'habitat': the natural environment in which a species lives. Virginia DWR and NPS Mount Rainier pre-activity handout (nps.gov/mora): shelter is one component of a habitat, alongside food, water and space. A bear's den versus its 30-square-mile range illustrates the difference in scale.

items.bewering: Party skuilings is natuurlik, en ander is deur mense gemaak. Die toets is elke keer dieselfde: wie of wat het dit gemaak? Dit gaan nie oor hoe die skuiling lyk of waarvan dit gemaak is nie.
items.bron: This is the classification convention, and it matches the lesson's own CAPS bullet, which lists nests, shells, hollow trees and wasp nests as natural and kennels, hokke, kraals and stalls as made by people. AskPhilosophers 22397 (askphilosophers.org) says the same: in everyday use a bird's nest or termite mound is natural and a human house is artificial, so the line is drawn by the maker and not by the material. 'Elke keer' was checked as an absolute. It holds for every example in the lesson.

items.bewering: 'n Voël wat 'n nes in 'n skuur bou, maak steeds 'n natuurlike skuiling. 'n Hondehok van hout is deur mense gemaak, al is hout self natuurlik.
items.bron: Follows from the maker test above (askphilosophers.org/node/22397). A review of urban birds (zrdc.ac.cn, doi 10.24272/j.issn.2097-3772.2024.009) confirms that birds nest on human-made structures. The nest is still the bird's work.

items.bewering: 'n Nes is 'n skuiling wat 'n dier self bou.
items.bron: Missouri Conservationist, 'Architects of the air' (mdc.mo.gov): nests are built by the animal from materials at hand. This is consistent with the maker test in the previous block.

items.bewering: Baie voëls dra takkies en wol aan om hul nes daarmee te bou.
items.bron: Missouri Conservationist, 'Architects of the air' (mdc.mo.gov): twigs and grass are the main materials. Overton Park Conservancy, 'NatureZen: love nests' (overtonpark.org): linings include hair and wool, and goldfinch nests are usually lined with wool. Twigs are near-universal and wool is a common lining, so 'baie' holds for the pair.

items.bewering: Muise en baie insekte bou ook neste, maar nie elke dier bou een nie.
items.bron: Bolton Council and Fylde Council pest guides (bolton.gov.uk, fylde.gov.uk): house mice build nests of shredded material, a round ball 10 to 15 cm across. Insect nests are confirmed by the wasp sources below and by honey bees nesting in tree cavities (Springer, J Insect Conserv, doi 10.1007/s10841-023-00530-7). The qualifier 'nie elke dier' is correct.

items.bewering: Baie perdebye kou ou droë hout sag en bou hul nes daarmee. Daardie gekoude hout word growwe grysbruin papier.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Paper wasp': they gather fibres from dead wood and plant stems, mix them with saliva, and build nests of grey or brown papery material. MFA CAMEO, 'Paper wasp' (cameo.mfa.org), and ATREE, 'Paper wasp: facts, nest, colony' (atree.org), say the same. 'Ou droë hout' is a fair Grade 4 rendering of 'dead wood'. 'Baie' is correct: paper wasps, hornets and yellowjackets, but not all wasps.

items.bewering: Party ander perdebye bou hul nes van klei.
items.bron: Utah State University Extension, 'Mason, potter and mud dauber wasps' (extension.usu.edu): potter wasps and mud daubers build nests of mud. Bug of the Week (bugoftheweek.com, 2017): clay soil is the female mud dauber's preferred mud. 'Klei' is acceptable for clay-rich mud.

items.bewering: 'n Skulp is 'n harde dop om die sagte lyf van 'n dier. 'n Tuinslak dra so 'n skulp op sy rug.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Land snail': the shell holds the visceral mass, and only the head and foot come out. Illinois DNR land snail document (dnr.illinois.gov, june09landsnails.pdf) agrees.

items.bewering: 'n Skulp word nie soos 'n nes gebou nie, maar groei saam met die dier as deel van sy lyf.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Land snail': the mantle secretes the shell, which grows by calcium carbonate added at the aperture. Illinois DNR (dnr.illinois.gov): the shell is permanently attached and the snail cannot crawl out of it. The columellar muscle anchors the body to the shell (biotopics.co.uk, 'Snail'). The claim is true of the snail the block names. A hermit crab's borrowed shell does not grow with it, but the lesson does not mention one.

items.bewering: 'n Hol boom is 'n boom met 'n oop gat binne sy stam. Voëls, vlermuise en bye maak dikwels daar hul huis.
items.bron: Ealing Council, 'Decaying wood' leaflet (ealing.gov.uk): owls, woodpeckers, nuthatches, tits and bats use rot holes. Missouri Department of Conservation (mdc.mo.gov): bees and bats use tree cavities. Springer, J Insect Conserv, doi 10.1007/s10841-023-00530-7, and PeerJ 4602: wild honey bee colonies naturally nest in cavity-bearing trees.

items.bewering: Insekte en swamme vreet die ou hout weg, maar gewoonlik maak geen mens daardie gat nie. 'n Hol boom bly dus 'n natuurlike skuiling.
items.bron: WA Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions journal (library.dbca.wa.gov.au, 080052-17.055): termites, fungi and micro-organisms eat away dead heartwood to form hollows. NSW EPA hollow-bearing trees document (epa.nsw.gov.au): fire, wind breakage and lightning also expose heartwood, so hollows are formed by natural processes. 'Vreet' is a Grade 4 rendering of fungal decay; the mapping holds. 'Gewoonlik ... geen mens' was checked as an absolute; the hedge is appropriate.

items.bewering: 'n Hondehok is 'n klein huisie wat mense vir 'n hond bou. Dit staan buite in die tuin en hou die hond droog en warm.
items.bron: Bunnings, 'DIY dog kennel' (bunnings.com.au), and Instructables, 'Dog kennel' (instructables.com): an outdoor timber shelter with a roof and walls to keep the dog out of the weather. 'Klein huisie' is a description, not a misleading analogy.

items.bewering: 'n Hok is 'n boks of 'n kamp met kante van draad of latte. Mense hou hoenders, hasies en voëls in hokke agter die huis. 'n Hok hou die dier binne, of dit hou gevaar buite.
items.bron: Merriam-Webster, 'hok' (African usage): a small enclosure or pen. Weiland's Dutch dictionary (dbnl.org) has hok as a fenced place for animals, as in duivenhok and hondenhok. For the local practice: South African household poultry studies record chickens kept by households, for example a mean of 10.9 birds per household across Limpopo, the Northern Cape and the Eastern Cape (sasas.co.za; uwcscholar.uwc.ac.za). City of Leduc backyard hen guidelines (leduc.ca) require coops to be predator-proof, which supports 'hou gevaar buite'. Limit: rabbits and birds rest on general rather than South African sources, but nothing contradicts them.

items.bewering: 'n Kraal is 'n oop kamp met 'n sterk heining rondom. Boere hou hul beeste, skape en bokke snags daar bymekaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Kraal', and Dictionary.com, 'kraal': an enclosure for cattle or other livestock in southern Africa, surrounded by a fence of thorn-bush branches, a palisade or a mud wall. Farmer's Weekly SA, 'Eco-friendly predator management' (farmersweekly.co.za): farmers had to kraal their flocks every night and are going back to night kraaling against predators and theft. Landmark Leopard and Predator Project (vantienhovenfoundation.com, Western Cape): kraaling livestock overnight reduces conflict with predators.

items.bewering: Party mense pak die heining van klip, en ander maak dit van takke met dorings.
items.bron: Stone: Klipriviersberg Heritage, 'Archaeology' (klipriviersberg.org.za), and Huffman et al., 'Stonewalling in the Klipriviersberg' (journals.uj.ac.za): stone-walled cattle kraals at the centre of Iron Age settlements. SAHRIS Free State history (sahris.sahra.org.za): stone kraals, and later farmers building their own kraals of stone. Thorn: Wikipedia, 'Kraal' (thorn-bush branches). The Botswana predator-safe livestock guide (hwctf.org) lists the thorn-branch kraal as one of the most common types.

items.bewering: 'n Stal is 'n gebou met mure en 'n dak. Perde en beeste staan binne in hul eie hokkies.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Stable': a building in which working animals, especially horses or oxen, are kept, usually divided into stalls. Wikipedia, 'Tie stall': individual tethered stalls are mostly used for dairy cows.

items.bewering: 'n Kraal het geen dak nie, maar 'n stal het wel een.
items.bron: Every kraal description found is a fenced or walled enclosure, open above: Wikipedia, 'Kraal'; the Klipriviersberg stone circles; the Botswana thorn kraals. A stable is a roofed building (Wikipedia, 'Stable'). 'Geen' was checked as an absolute and holds for the meaning of the word.

items.bewering: 'n Struktuur is iets wat gebou of gevorm is en wat sy eie vorm hou. Dit val nie inmekaar wanneer jy daaraan stoot of iets daarop sit nie. 'n Struktuur dra iets swaars, of dit hou iets daarbinne veilig.
items.bron: Education Quizzes KS2 D&T, 'Structures' (educationquizzes.com): a built framework or shape that supports weight and holds its form. Ingenium Canada, 'Stable structures' kit: strength is the ability to hold a load. Manitoba Education, Grade 7 Science cluster 3 (edu.gov.mb.ca): structures support, contain or protect. 'Val nie inmekaar nie' is the standard primary definition, 'supports a load without collapsing'. It implies the load the structure is meant to carry, not any push at all. It is not flagged, but a writer touching this block should not make it more absolute.

items.bewering: 'n Nes, 'n skulp en 'n stal is almal strukture.
items.bron: Kapow Primary, 'Pupil video: shell structures' (kapowprimary.com): natural shells such as a tortoise shell or eggshell are taught as structures. Education Quizzes KS2 (educationquizzes.com) lists shelters as structures. Each item meets the lesson's own definition: built or formed, holds its shape, and protects or carries.

items.bewering: 'n Dopstruktuur het een dun buitekant wat om die binnekant sit. Daardie buitekant hou self sy vorm sonder 'n raam daarbinne. Dit kry sy sterkte uit sy vorm en nie uit sy dikte nie.
items.bron: Brick&Bolt, 'Shell structure' (bricknbolt.com): a shell is a thin, curved plate that gets its strength mainly from its shape rather than its material thickness, and carries loads through its shape rather than internal framing. RevisionDojo IB Design Technology A3.2.2 (revisiondojo.com): the thin, curved outer surface carries the load. The IntechOpen chapter on bio-inspired shells (intechopen.com/chapters/83586) says the same.

items.bewering: 'n Tuinslak se skulp is 'n dopstruktuur, want sy dun wand hou sy eie vorm om die slak.
items.bron: The IntechOpen chapter on bio-inspired shells (intechopen.com/chapters/83586) and the university shell lecture it cites list seashells and turtle shells as natural shell structures. Kapow Primary (kapowprimary.com) teaches tortoise shells and eggshells as shell structures. A snail shell is a one-piece, thin, curved, hollow wall with no internal frame. The columella is part of the shell itself, not a frame inside it.

items.bewering: Die nes wat party perdebye van klei bou, is ook 'n dop met 'n dun wand.
items.bron: Brisbane Insects, 'Mud dauber / yellow potter wasp' (brisbaneinsects.com): a dome-shaped mud pot about 15 mm across, built from mud balls about 2 mm in diameter. The historical account on archive.org (biostor-149259) says Eumenes spread flat plates of mud and curl them into a saucer, a bowl and then a narrow-mouthed pot. The ISSMGE paper 'Fabric and structure of potter wasp nests' (issmge.org) analyses the nest as a load-bearing shell by finite elements. No source gives a wall thickness in millimetres; 'thin' is inferred from a 15 mm pot built of 2 mm pellets and the same paper notes the thickness varies. That is enough for 'party perdebye', which the potter wasp's pot satisfies. Do not widen this to every mud nest: mud daubers often cover their cells with thick lumps of mud (archive.org account of Eumenes covering cell groups).

items.bewering: 'n Raamstruktuur is los dele wat aanmekaar sit met oop plekke tussen hulle.
items.bron: Woodside Primary, 'Y1 and Y2 DT knowledge organiser: freestanding structures' (woodside.gloucs.sch.uk): a frame structure is made of different parts joined together. Kaikki/Wiktionary, 'framework': joined parts with intervening open spaces. RevisionDojo A3.2.2 (revisiondojo.com): a skeleton of connected members. Note: RevisionDojo warns that classification is by load path, not merely by empty space. The lesson's definition rests on 'los dele wat aanmekaar sit', which carries that, so it does not misclassify a one-piece shell with holes.

items.bewering: 'n Hoenderhok van latte en draad is 'n raamstruktuur. Die latte en die draad is aan mekaar vasgemaak, met oop plekke tussen die drade.
items.bron: Classed by form, a coop of slats and wire is separate members joined with open spaces, which is a frame (RevisionDojo A3.2.2; Woodside Primary knowledge organiser). Tested against the set: a coop's wire mesh carries no weight and does the job a covering does, so a strict reader could call a coop 'a frame with a covering', as the next block calls a kennel. The lesson classifies by form, and a mesh coop stays open members on every face, unlike a planked kennel. Not flagged, but this is the seam to protect if either block is revised.

items.bewering: Die raam van hout binne 'n hondehok is ook 'n raamstruktuur.
items.bron: Bunnings, 'DIY dog kennel' (bunnings.com.au): treated-pine front, side and back frames with studs. Instructables, 'Dog kennel' (instructables.com): a 3x2 timber framework with cladding nailed on. This block does not qualify the claim; the next block adds 'dikwels', which is the accurate form, because some commercial kennels are assembled from panels (Summer Garden Buildings kits).

items.bewering: Party skuilings is 'n raam met 'n bedekking daaroor. 'n Hondehok het dikwels 'n raam van hout met planke daaroor. Die raam dra die gewig en hou die hondehok regop. Die planke is 'n bedekking wat die reën uithou. So 'n hondehok is 'n raamstruktuur met 'n bedekking.
items.blok: Nie elke skuiling pas in een groep nie
items.bron: Instructables (instructables.com) and Bunnings (bunnings.com.au) kennel builds: a timber frame clad with boards, plus a roof. RevisionDojo, 'Frame, shell, solid, combination structures' (revisiondojo.com): many buildings combine a frame that supports with an outer skin. 'Dikwels' is correctly hedged.

items.bewering: 'n Kraal van klip is nie 'n raam of 'n dop nie, maar 'n dik muur. Nie elke skuiling pas dus netjies in een van die twee groepe nie.
items.blok: Nie elke skuiling pas in een groep nie
items.bron: RevisionDojo IB DT A3.2.2 (revisiondojo.com) and Manitoba Education, Grade 7 structures (edu.gov.mb.ca): technology classifies structures as solid (mass), frame and shell, so a solid stone wall is the third type and not a frame or a shell. Designing Buildings Wiki, 'A history of stone walling' (designingbuildings.co.uk): dry-stone walls stand by their mass. Tested as a set with the shell and frame examples: the snail shell and the clay pot get strength from their shape, the coop and the kennel frame are joined members, the kennel is a combination, and the stone kraal is mass. The contrast with 'sterkte uit sy vorm en nie uit sy dikte nie' is consistent. 'Nie elke ... netjies' was checked as a quantifier and is correct.

items.bewering: Baie voëlneste is soos 'n diep koppie wat die eiers binnehou as die tak waai.
items.bron: Overton Park, 'NatureZen: love nests' (overtonpark.org): a deep cup keeps the eggs from rolling or falling out. The Auk 94(4):646-651 (sora.unm.edu): small species build narrow, deep cups. MIT OCW bird-nest notes (ocw.mit.edu): the common nest is hemispherical inside, with a rim several egg-diameters high. The cup comparison is mapped correctly to shape and function: it holds its contents when tilted. 'Baie' is right, since many nests are platforms, burrows or domes.

items.bewering: 'n Tuinslak se skulp draai in 'n ronde krul waarin die slak diep kan wegkruip.
items.bron: Biotopics, 'Snail' (biotopics.co.uk): the columellar muscle pulls the whole body inside the coiled shell. Illinois DNR (dnr.illinois.gov): snails withdraw deeply and seal the opening during dry or cold spells. Wikipedia, 'Land snail': the coiled shell.

items.bewering: Skuilings is ook nie almal ewe groot nie. Baie voëlneste pas in jou twee hande.
items.bron: PLOS ONE 6(4):e19086, table 1 (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3084263): measured outside diameters are about 11 to 12 cm for American robin nests and 6 to 8 cm for warbler, redpoll and sparrow nests. All fit in two cupped hands. 'Baie' is correctly hedged, given large nests such as eagles' and sociable weavers'.

items.bewering: 'n Hondehok is groot genoeg vir een hond om in te lê. 'n Kraal is baie groter as 'n hondehok, want 'n hele trop beeste moet daar inpas.
items.bron: Bunnings kennel plan (bunnings.com.au): sized to a single dog. Klipriviersberg Heritage (klipriviersberg.org.za) and Huffman et al. (journals.uj.ac.za): a central cattle enclosure holds a herd. The comparative 'baie groter' was checked and follows from cattle size and herd numbers.

items.bewering: Gras en takkies is lig genoeg vir 'n voël om na sy nes te dra.
items.bron: Missouri Conservationist, 'Architects of the air' (mdc.mo.gov): birds carry grasses and twigs to the nest site, one beakful at a time.

items.bewering: Klip hou jare lank, en 'n klipmuur om 'n kraal staan stewig.
items.bron: Sadr, Leiden ASC lecture (ascleiden.nl/pdf/papersadr.pdf): Iron Age stone-walled livestock enclosures of the second millennium AD still stand across the subcontinent. The Mail & Guardian, 14 November 2013 ('Walking in the ruins of a lost world'), dates these stone kraals to before the 1830s. 'Jare lank' understates this, which is safe.

items.bewering: Klei droog hard uit en hou 'n perdeby se nes stewig.
items.bron: Bug of the Week, 20 February 2023 (bugoftheweek.com): mud dauber nests harden into durable 'pottery' that survives for years. Utah State University Extension (extension.usu.edu): the mud nests stay firmly attached to walls.

items.bewering: Hout is sterk en maklik om te saag, daarom bou mense hondehokke daarvan.
items.bron: Bunnings (bunnings.com.au) and Instructables (instructables.com) kennel builds, and the Summer Garden Buildings kits (summergardenbuildings.co.uk): kennels are commonly built of sawn timber cut to size. The reason given is a fair, simple one and is not presented as the only reason.

items.bewering: skuiling: 'n Plek wat 'n dier teen gevaar of teen die weer beskerm.
items.bron: Virginia DWR (dwr.virginia.gov): protection from weather and predators. Read alone, it is accurate. It matches the study block.

items.bewering: habitat: Die plek waar 'n plant of 'n dier lewe.
items.bron: Vocabulary.com, 'habitat': the natural environment in which a species lives, applied to plants and animals. Read alone, it is accurate. In its block the study text adds 'die hele plek', which the entry does not contradict.

items.bewering: struktuur: Iets wat gebou of gevorm is, sy vorm hou en gewig dra of iets beskerm.
items.bron: Education Quizzes KS2 (educationquizzes.com) and Manitoba Education Grade 7 (edu.gov.mb.ca): structures hold their form and support, contain or protect. Read alone, it is accurate and slightly safer than the study block, because it has no 'val nie inmekaar nie'.

items.bewering: dopstruktuur: 'n Dun buitekant wat om die binnekant sit en sonder 'n raam sy vorm hou. Dit kry sy sterkte uit sy vorm en nie uit sy dikte nie.
items.bron: Brick&Bolt (bricknbolt.com) and RevisionDojo (revisiondojo.com): thin, curved, strength from shape, no internal framing. Read alone, it is accurate.

items.bewering: raamstruktuur: Los dele wat aanmekaar sit met oop plekke tussen hulle.
items.bron: Woodside Primary knowledge organiser (woodside.gloucs.sch.uk): parts joined together. Kaikki/Wiktionary 'framework': joined parts and open spaces. Read alone, it says nothing about load. That is acceptable at Grade 4 because the 'struktuur' entry supplies it, but it is the thinnest of the definitions.

items.bewering: skulp: 'n Harde dop wat om die sagte lyf van 'n dier soos 'n slak groei.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Land snail', and Illinois DNR (dnr.illinois.gov): the mantle secretes the shell around the soft body and it grows with the animal. Read alone, it is accurate for molluscs. 'Soos 'n slak' anchors it to the right kind of animal.

items.bewering: perdebynes: Die nes wat baie perdebye van gekoude hout bou, en party ander van klei.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Paper wasp' (chewed wood fibre), and Utah State University Extension (extension.usu.edu; mud). Read alone, it is accurate and the quantifiers match the study block.

items.bewering: kraal: 'n Oop kamp met 'n heining waar boere hul vee bymekaarhou.
items.bron: Dictionary.com, 'kraal', sense 1: an enclosure for cattle and other domestic animals in southern Africa. Wikipedia, 'Kraal'. Read alone, it is accurate for the sense used. The word also has a 'homestead or village' sense, which the lesson does not use.

items.bewering: stal: 'n Gebou met mure en 'n dak waar perde of beeste staan.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Stable': a building for working animals, especially horses or oxen. Read alone, it is accurate.

items.bewering: materiaal: Die goed waarvan iets gemaak is, soos hout of klip.
items.bron: This is the standard dictionary sense: the substance a thing is made of (Merriam-Webster, 'material', sense 1). Read alone, it is accurate. The examples are consistent with the materials list.

items.bewering: Vraag 1, implied answer: a bird's nest built in an old tractor in a shed is natural.
items.bron: Consistent with the maker test (askphilosophers.org/node/22397) and with the study block on a nest in a barn.

items.bewering: Vraag 2, implied answer: of a wire chicken coop and a snail's shell, the coop is the frame structure.
items.bron: Consistent with the frame and shell sources above (RevisionDojo, Woodside Primary, IntechOpen). The mesh-as-covering seam noted on the coop item applies here too.

items.bewering: Vraag 3, implied answer: a cattle kraal must be much bigger than a kennel.
items.bron: Same sources as the size item: Klipriviersberg Heritage (klipriviersberg.org.za) and the Bunnings kennel plan (bunnings.com.au).

opsomming: Every checkable claim was confirmed against sources and nothing needs correcting. The shelters and the shell/frame/thick-wall examples hold together when tested as a set. There are no literal superlatives, and the absolutes and comparatives were checked as superlatives. Two seams should be protected if the text is revised: 'thin wall' fits a potter wasp's pot but not every mud nest, and the coop's wire mesh could be read as a covering. The lesson still carries three question blocks, which is outside a fact check.
